Elliptic unit

Words: 100 Articles: 1
Algebraic number theory OurBigBook.com
Elliptic units are algebraic units constructed by evaluating suitably normalized elliptic functions at CM torsion points and taking products or norms into ray class fields. Their distribution relations make them norm compatible in CM division towers. They generate an Euler system of elliptic units and their local Coleman power series for a CM formal group have logarithmic derivatives encoding critical Hecke L-function values.

Euler system of elliptic units

Words: 52
Elliptic unit OurBigBook.com
Elliptic-unit distribution gives norm-compatible units indexed by auxiliary squarefree ray moduli, with norm factor 1−Frobq−1​ at a newly added prime. Kolyvagin derivative operators turn these units into classes with controlled valuations, and suitable auxiliary primes chosen using Chebotarev density theorem bound class-group characteristic ideals. The construction supplies the difficult divisibility in the CM Iwasawa main conjecture.

Hecke character

Words: 271 Articles: 3
Algebraic number theory OurBigBook.com
A Hecke character of a number field is a continuous character of its idèle class group. Its finite conductor records the local unit subgroups on which it is trivial. As an ideal character it is defined on fractional ideals prime to that conductor, with a prescribed rule on principal ideals coming from its archimedean character. A CM elliptic curve yields an algebraic Hecke character with one CM embedding in its infinity type of a Hecke character.

Hecke character of a CM elliptic curve (ψE​:AF×​/F×→C×)

Words: 150 Articles: 1
Hecke character OurBigBook.com
Suppose F contains the CM field K and all CM endomorphisms are defined over F. CM reciprocity compares the torus with its idele-transformed lattice and gives a(s)∈K× for finite ideles. Then ψE​(s)=a(sf​)/NF/K​(s)∞​. On principal ideles, a(bf​)=NF/K​(b), so the character descends to the idèle class group. At a good prime its ideal value reduces to the Frobenius isogeny. If the original field omits K, construct the character over FK and induce the corresponding representation down to the original field.

Grössencharacter of the square-lattice elliptic curve (ψE​(a)=the primary generator of a)

Words: 72
Hecke character of a CM elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
For E:y2=x3−x over Q(i), the Hecke character has conductor (1+i)3 and ideal infinity type (1,0). Its value on an ideal prime to 2 is its unique primary Gaussian integer generator. Rational (1+i)3-torsion fixes the unit ambiguity of the Frobenius value. At a split prime p, its value reduces to the degree-p Frobenius isogeny; at an inert rational prime p, its value is −p, reducing to the p2-power Frobenius isogeny.

Infinity type of a Hecke character

Words: 57
Hecke character OurBigBook.com
For an algebraic Hecke character, the character on archimedean ideles is a product of integral powers of embeddings and their complex conjugates. In the convention ψ((a))=a for primary a over an imaginary quadratic field, the ideal character has type (1,0) and the idele character has archimedean component z−1. Distinguishing these conventions avoids inverse errors in CM Galois representations.

Kummer-Dedekind theorem

Words: 155 Articles: 2
Algebraic number theory OurBigBook.com
The factorization of a defining polynomial modulo a prime, provided the index is coprime to that prime, determines the prime ideals, ramification indices and residue degrees in the corresponding ring of integers.

Squarefree reduction excludes a prime from the power-basis index (f​ squarefree⟹p∤[OK​:Z[α]])

Words: 41
Kummer-Dedekind theorem OurBigBook.com
For an algebraic integer α generating a number field, the polynomial discriminant of its minimal polynomial f equals the discriminant of elements of a number field for its power basis. A squarefree reduction modulo p has nonzero resultant with its derivative, so p∤disc(f). The discriminant-index formula for an integral lattice, disc(f)=[OK​:Z[α]]2dK​, proves the assertion.

Quotient-ring proof of the Kummer-Dedekind theorem (OK​/pOK​≃Fp​[X]/(m))

Words: 82
Kummer-Dedekind theorem OurBigBook.com
For an integral generator α of a number field, let A=Z[α] and suppose p is coprime to [OK​:A]. Localizing at p makes A and the ring of integers equal, so reduction gives the displayed quotient ring. If m=∏giei​​ with distinct monic irreducible polynomials, the Chinese remainder theorem gives local factors Fp​[X]/(giei​​). Their residue fields have degrees deggi​ and their maximal ideals have nilpotence indices of an ideal ei​. Localizing the Dedekind domain OK​ at the corresponding prime ideals gives discrete valuation rings, where this same nilpotence index of an ideal is the ramification index of a prime ideal. Thus (p)=∏(p,gi​(α))ei​ and each residue degree is deggi​.

Leopoldt conjecture (δF,p​=0)

Words: 96 Articles: 1
Algebraic number theory OurBigBook.com
The Leopoldt conjecture says that the diagonal image of the global units of a number field in its local p-adic unit groups has Zp​-rank r1​+r2​−1. A defect would measure a loss of rank after p-adic completion. It is a theorem for abelian extensions of Q.

Leopoldt theorem for abelian number fields

Words: 46
Leopoldt conjecture OurBigBook.com
The Leopoldt conjecture holds for every finite abelian extension of Q. The proof uses linear independence of p-adic logarithms of algebraic numbers. In cyclotomic towers it supplies the ranks of the global-unit terms in the class-field unit sequence; it is not needed for the unramified Iwasawa torsion theorem in arbitrary towers.

Iwasawa theory

Words: 2k Articles: 37
Algebraic number theory OurBigBook.com
Iwasawa theory studies arithmetic objects in infinite towers of number fields, often Zp-extensions. Passing to inverse limits turns growing ideal class groups, unit groups and Galois groups into modules over an Iwasawa algebra. Their algebraic ranks and characteristic ideals organize the growth and relate it to p-adic L-functions.

Main conjecture of Iwasawa theory

Words: 286 Articles: 4
Iwasawa theory OurBigBook.com
The classical Iwasawa main conjecture, now a theorem over Q, identifies characteristic ideals of appropriate cyclotomic Iwasawa modules with ideals generated by p-adic L-function power series. For a nontrivial even character in the p-ramified convention, charΛ​Xχ​=(gχ​) with gχ​((1+p)1−s−1)=Lp​(χ,s). The Kummer reflection in Iwasawa theory accounts for the reflected odd class-group convention.

Characteristic-ideal bridge from local units to the main conjecture (char(E/C)char(X)=char(U/C)char(Y))

Words: 71
Main conjecture of Iwasawa theory OurBigBook.com
In the real cyclotomic tower, the class-field unit sequence gives 0→E/C→U/C→X→Y→0, where X is the p-ramified Iwasawa module and Y the unramified one. The modules are torsion over each one-variable character component. Splitting the four-term sequence into two short exact sequences proves the displayed identity by multiplicativity of characteristic ideals. The Iwasawa theorem on local cyclotomic units computes char(U/C) analytically. Thus the main conjecture for X is equivalent to char(E/C)=char(Y); local interpolation alone does not prove this remaining global equality.

Iwasawa theorem on local cyclotomic units (U∞1​/C∞1​≃Zp​[[G]]/(I(G)ζp​))

Words: 64
Main conjecture of Iwasawa theory OurBigBook.com
For the real p-power cyclotomic tower, take norm limits of local principal units and closed cyclotomic-unit subgroups. The corrected Coleman logarithm identifies U∞1​ with the Iwasawa algebra of G=Zp×​/{±1}. On a symmetric cyclotomic unit it gives ([b]−[a])ζp​. A topological generator generates the cyclotomic-unit limit and the augmentation ideal, yielding the quotient description. This local calculation does not alone identify the characteristic ideal of the global Galois module.

One-variable main conjecture for CM elliptic curves (charΛ​Xχ​=(Lχ​))

Words: 74
Main conjecture of Iwasawa theory OurBigBook.com
At a good split prime, the one-prime CM division tower has a pro-p Galois group isomorphic to Zp​. Its prime-ramified Iwasawa module is torsion on each finite-character component. The main conjecture identifies its characteristic ideal with the corresponding elliptic-unit p-adic L-function. The class-field unit sequence and equality of characteristic ideals of global-units modulo elliptic-units and of class groups prove the identification. The cyclotomic Selmer formulation requires the appropriate CM twist and two-variable specialization; the one-prime tower is not the cyclotomic tower.

Mazur-Wiles theorem

Words: 31
Main conjecture of Iwasawa theory OurBigBook.com
The Mazur-Wiles theorem proves the classical Iwasawa main conjecture for abelian extensions of Q. Its construction of class fields uses Galois representations associated with modular forms, congruences with Eisenstein series and the Eisenstein ideal.

Iwasawa module

Words: 2k Articles: 27
Iwasawa theory OurBigBook.com
An Iwasawa module is a module over an Iwasawa algebra. In arithmetic towers it usually comes from a norm inverse limit of units or class groups, or from a compact Galois module for a maximal abelian pro-p extension. Specify which extension is allowed to ramify: the p-ramified Iwasawa module and the unramified Iwasawa module have different ranks.

p-ramified Iwasawa module (X=Gal(M∞​/F∞​))

Words: 1k Articles: 17
Iwasawa module OurBigBook.com
Let M∞​ be the maximal abelian pro-p extension of F∞​ unramified away from primes over p. Its Galois group is the p-ramified Iwasawa module. In the cyclotomic tower of Q(μp​) for odd p, its Iwasawa-module rank is (p−1)/2. It is therefore quite different from the torsion unramified Iwasawa module.
Class-field unit sequence (0→E∞​→U∞​→X→Y→0)
Words: 1k Articles: 16
p-ramified Iwasawa module OurBigBook.com
Passing to norm limits in Artin reciprocity gives an exact sequence connecting closures of global units, local pro-p units at primes over p, the p-ramified Iwasawa module and the unramified Iwasawa module. It explains arithmetic Iwasawa-module ranks by comparing local and global unit ranks. Roots of unity and the precise splitting conventions must be retained when seeking exact integral statements.
Coleman power series (fu​(T))
Words: 1k Articles: 15
Class-field unit sequence OurBigBook.com
A Coleman power series encodes a norm-compatible sequence of local units in a cyclotomic tower by a single integral power series evaluated at ζpn​−1. A logarithmic derivative and trace correction give a measure, relating the local images of cyclotomic units to p-adic L-functions.
Coleman interpolation theorem for cyclotomic local units (fu​(ζn​−1)=un​,Nfu​=fu​)
Words: 104
Coleman power series OurBigBook.com
For odd p and a norm-compatible sequence of local units in Qp​(μpn+1​), there is a unique fu​∈Zp​[[T]]× interpolating all its entries, and the Coleman norm operator fixes it. To construct it, choose integral unit polynomials Fj​ interpolating entry uj​, and take a convergent subsequence of NjF2j​ in the compact (p,T)-adic unit space. The congruence NF≡F(modp) and Coleman norm contraction show that its evaluation at any fixed level tends to the desired entry. Uniqueness follows from the Weierstrass preparation theorem: a nonzero integral power series has only finitely many zeros in the open unit disk. The norm relation on evaluations then proves norm fixation. Principal units correspond to fu​(0)≡1(modp).

Zp-extension OurBigBook.com
At least one finite prime ramifies in a Zp-extension; otherwise the entire tower would lie in a finite Hilbert class field. Ramification can occur only over p: local class field theory makes inertia away from p an image of a unit group with finite maximal pro-p quotient, whereas Zp​ has no nontrivial finite subgroup. Nonzero inertia is open in Zp​, so it becomes total after passing to a sufficiently high finite layer.

Hermite–Minkowski theorem

Words: 171 Articles: 1
Algebraic number theory OurBigBook.com
For fixed degree and bounded absolute discriminant, there are only finitely many number fields up to isomorphism. In particular, only finitely many extensions of bounded degree can be unramified outside a fixed finite set of primes when their ramification exponents are bounded.

Bounded-degree extensions with restricted ramification

Words: 129
Hermite–Minkowski theorem OurBigBook.com
Fix a number field K, a positive integer d, and a finite set S of its finite places. There are finitely many field extensions L/K of degree at most d unramified outside S, inside a fixed algebraic closure. To see this, view them as extensions of the rational numbers of bounded degree. Their ramified rational primes belong to a fixed finite set. At each of these primes, the different exponent is bounded in terms of the local degree and ramification index, giving a bound for the absolute field discriminant. The Hermite–Minkowski theorem gives finitely many fields up to isomorphism, and each has only finitely many embeddings into the fixed closure. This useful form of arithmetic compactness is stated and proved for K=Q in Andrew Sutherland's number-theory notes, Theorem 14.25; the preceding reduction gives the general case.

An arbitrary totally imaginary number field need not have such a real subfield of index two.

Only the inertia group invariants enter an Artin L-function local factor. A Frobenius automorphism lift acts unambiguously on this subspace, since other lifts differ by inertia. For an unramified one-dimensional group representation, the factor is (1−χ(Frobp​)(Np)−s)−1; for a ramified one-dimensional group representation, the invariant subspace is zero and the factor is one. Artin L-function OurBigBook.com
Assume that every nontrivial one-dimensional Artin L-function over the intermediate fields is holomorphic and nonzero at one, while the trivial one is the base Dedekind zeta function with a simple pole. By Brauer induction, χ=∑j​nj​IndHj​G​ψj​ with integers nj​ and linear characters ψj​. Compatibility of Artin L-functions with induced representations expresses LK​(χ,s) as the corresponding product of LLHj​​(ψj​,s)nj​. Its order at one is −∑j​nj​⟨ψj​,1Hj​​⟩. Frobenius reciprocity turns this sum into −⟨χ,1G​⟩. Hence every nontrivial irreducible character gives order zero and a holomorphic nonzero function near one. This local conclusion does not assert global Artin holomorphy.

Modulus of a number field OurBigBook.com
For a modulus of a number field c=c0​c∞​, the multiplicity at a finite place is the exponent of its prime ideal in c0​. Artin reciprocity law

Words: 204 Articles: 2
Artin symbol OurBigBook.com
The Artin map sends an ideal prime to the ramified primes to the product of its Frobenius elements. For a suitable modulus, its kernel is the norm or congruence subgroup associated with the abelian extension.
Idelic local-global reciprocity equivalence (θL/K​((av​))=∏v​recv​(av​))
Words: 91
Artin reciprocity law OurBigBook.com
For a finite abelian extension of number fields, local reciprocity maps into the local decomposition groups combine to a continuous map on the idele group: outside finitely many places they kill units, and an idele has nonunit components only finitely often. The Artin reciprocity law is equivalent to the compatibility that this product kills every principal idele. Conversely, restrict a global continuous Artin homomorphism to each single-place embedding of Kv∗​. These maps reconstruct the global map, by density of finite-component ideles and triviality on a basic open subgroup of units. Merely having unrelated local maps omits the essential principal-idele compatibility.

Words: 78
Artin reciprocity law OurBigBook.com
For an abelian extension L/K of number fields, restriction to an intermediate field takes each Artin symbol to that of the smaller extension. For a finite base extension E/K, restriction identifies Gal(LE/E) with Gal(L/(L∩E)). At an unramified prime q of E above p, its residue-field Frobenius restricts to the f(q/p)th power of the Frobenius automorphism at p. Since NE/K​q=pf(q/p), the group homomorphism property proves the displayed identity for fractional ideals supported over unramified primes.

Conductor of an abelian extension

Words: 100 Articles: 1
Class field theory OurBigBook.com
The conductor fL/K​ is the smallest modulus through which the Artin reciprocity map for a finite abelian extension L/K factors. Its finite prime divisors are exactly the ramified primes, with exponents measuring the depth of ramification.

Conductor-discriminant formula (dL/K​=∏χ​f(χ))

Words: 66
Conductor of an abelian extension OurBigBook.com
For a finite abelian extension of number fields, its relative discriminant ideal is the product of the finite conductor ideals of the characters of its Galois group, with the trivial character contributing one. In a multiquadratic extension of Q, the nontrivial characters correspond to its quadratic subfields, and their conductors are the absolute values of the corresponding fundamental discriminants. This gives an efficient discriminant computation and can prove that a compositum is unramified over a quadratic subfield.

Ray class field of Q of square root minus six modulo square root minus six (K(−6​)​=Q(2​,−3​))
Words: 81
Ray class field OurBigBook.com
For K=Q(−6​), reduction of Z[−6​] modulo (−6​) gives Z/6Z. Its unit group is covered by the units {1,−1} of K. The ray class exact sequence therefore identifies the ray class group with the ordinary ideal class group, of order two. Consequently this ray class field is the Hilbert class field of Q of square root minus six. To verify its lack of ramification, the integral basis candidate 1,2​,b,2​b, where b=(1+−3​)/2, has discriminant 82(−3)2=576. The relative discriminant formula also forces the field discriminant to be divisible by (−24)2=576. Equality proves that the relative discriminant ideal is trivial.
Ray class field of Q of square root minus three modulo seven (K(7)​=Q(ζ21​),K=Q(−3​))
Words: 72
Ray class field OurBigBook.com
The ring of integers is Z[ω], where ω2+ω+1=0, and its class number is one by the Minkowski bound for ideal classes. Modulo seven it is F7​×F7​. The six roots of unity reduce to the kernel of the product map on the two residue unit groups, so the ray class group is F7×​, of order six. The relative Artin symbol on K(ζ7​) is exponentiation by the norm of a fractional ideal modulo seven. It kills the principal ray subgroup, and [K(ζ7​):K]=6, proving that this is the ray class field.

Ray class field OurBigBook.com
For a positive integer m, the finite ray class group of Q is (Z/mZ)×/⟨−1⟩: the unit group permits either sign of a rational generator. Its ray class field is the maximal real subfield of the cyclotomic field Q(ζm​). Including the real place requires positive principal generators and gives the full group (Z/mZ)× and full cyclotomic field. Thus modulus (5) gives Q(5​), while (5)∞ gives Q(ζ5​). The Artin reciprocity map sends a prime ℓ∤m to the exponent ℓ, taken modulo {±1} in the finite case. Ramification at real places is possible only when those places are included in the modulus of a number field.

Hilbert class field OurBigBook.com
For a CM-field K over its maximal real subfield K+, the ordinary Hilbert class field HK+​ is totally real because its real places split. Thus HK+​∩K=K+. Words: 78
Hilbert class field OurBigBook.com
The three reduced primitive binary quadratic forms of discriminant −23 are (1,1,6) and (2,±1,3), so the class number is three. The displayed cubic has discriminant −23 and is irreducible. Its splitting field has Galois group S3​ and is cyclic cubic over Q(−23​). Modulo 23 it factors as (X−10)2(X−3). Lift the simple factor; the remaining quadratic has discriminant valuation one, so its local inertia group has order two. Its intersection with A3​ is trivial. Thus the relative cyclic cubic extension is everywhere unramified and equals the Hilbert class field.

Hilbert class field OurBigBook.com
The polynomial is irreducible with discriminant 229, so its splitting field has Galois group S3​ and quadratic subfield Q(229​). The splitting field is cyclic cubic over that subfield. It is unramified outside 229, and at 229 its inertia is a transposition, meeting the alternating cubic subgroup trivially. All roots are real. It is therefore everywhere unramified over the quadratic field. The ideal class group of Q of square root 229 has order three, so this extension is exactly the Hilbert class field.

Let K have degree n, and suppose a rational prime p factors into n distinct prime ideals of norm p. If n>p, then K is not monogenic. Otherwise the Dedekind factorization theorem would force the degree-n minimal polynomial of a power-basis generator to have n distinct linear factors over Fp​, although only the p polynomials X−a are available.

Dedekind zeta function as a permutation Artin L-function (ζK​(s)=LQ​(C[Hom(K,E)],s))

Words: 105
Dedekind zeta function OurBigBook.com
Let E be a finite normal closure of the number field K. The permutation representation of its Galois group on the embeddings of K into E has one trivial constituent, because the action is transitive. At a prime, the inertia group invariant basis consists of sums over inertia orbits of embeddings; Frobenius automorphism permutes them in cycles of lengths equal to the residue degrees of the primes of K. A cycle of length f contributes det(1−Tρ(Frob))=1−Tf. Hence the local factors equal those of the Dedekind zeta function, including at ramified primes. If nontrivial irreducible Artin L-functions are holomorphic and nonzero at one, this factorization and the simple pole of the Riemann zeta function show that ζK​ has a simple pole there.

For a quadratic field K of discriminant D,
ζK​(s)=ζQ​(s)L(χD​,s),
(74)
where χD​(p) is 1, −1, or 0 according as (p) splits, remains prime, or ramifies in OK​. Comparing the three possible local Euler factors proves the formal identity.
